Seat increment (re-read at `origin/main` `ded67bfb`, 2026-10-29T10:17Z):
- Premises re-run, all hold: an unchanged MCP instance is not reconnected on reconcile (plugin.ts L1844–1847), so a running process holds no earlier good snapshot; the degraded channel is `degradeConnectorInstance` (plugin.ts L2172, called L2077) and its wording describes an unavailable upstream; `toolsSnapshot` has 0 hits under `packages/` (nothing shipped yet); item 1 (`openapi` `include`, PR #27387) is merged and not held by this card; #27373 (the offline normalisation tool the card names as a pin emitter) is closed.
- Prior rulings: triage 6487372008 graded the item (protocol addition, p1, `domain:server`) and ruled nothing on the shape; `check-prior-rulings.mjs --card 27401` names ADR-0129 D3, ADR-0097 §6, ADR-0109 §4, ADR-0032 — term matches, none decides a snapshot pin's granularity. The item's own acceptance line ("a message naming the changed tool") is the governing text, and it contradicts the item's key shape (one aggregate hash); the maintainer picks which half gives way.
- Facets: agree with the card on all four. ① per-tool integrity, keyed by tool name like `include`, is the lockfile shape (npm / pnpm record integrity per package, not one hash per tree); the two keys compose. ② no customer named it; the item is inside the scope the maintainer directed on 2026-10-27 (「建议 1+2立卡」), so D is the exit if that scope is withdrawn, not the default. ③ B names the tool and distinguishes "pin stale" from "tool rewritten"; A compresses both into one undiagnosable message; C hides state in process history. ④ A and B cost the same (one helper + tests); neither adds a gate.
- Seat's letter: **B** — `providerConfig.toolsSnapshot`, a record keyed by tool name whose value is the sha256 of that tool's canonical `name` + `description` + `inputSchema`; a mismatch degrades the instance with a message naming the tool (and a pinned tool that is gone); the aggregate `toolsSnapshotSha256` spelling is retired before it ever ships. Carry the card's confidence gap into the dispatch: the degraded channel's "upstream unavailable … retrying with backoff" wording and retry loop should be specialised for a pin mismatch (no reconnect loop fixes a pin).
- Workload of B: `domain:server` · 1 PR · S–M · `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` ⇒ contract review before landing · no precedent.
- After the ruling: the #27293 epic PM dispatches it to `domain:server` with `Ruling-ref:`; the card leaves the box under `pm:epic` (its stroke).
